patch.value: closeout cannot close items in trackers that require structured close fields

Found while dogfooding pm github closeout on 2026-10-15. pm-rust's tracker enforces strict close validation, so pm close requires resolution, expected_result and actual_result. closeout passes only a close reason, so pm github closeout --apply on pm-rust PR 81 failed on the first item ('missing resolution, expected_result, actual_result'), wrote nothing (it failed closed) and left all seven delivered items open; the orchestrator closed them by hand. closeout should populate the structured fields from the same verifiable GitHub facts it already uses (resolution: delivered by the PR, with merge and head SHAs; expected_result: the item's acceptance criteria when present; actual_result: merged, with the passing required checks), never from PR body or comment text, and should report clearly when a tracker policy still refuses the close.

On a tracker with strict close validation, closeout --apply closes every eligible item with resolution, expected_result and actual_result derived only from GitHub facts and the item's own acceptance criteria; the fields contain no PR body or comment text; a tracker that refuses the close for another reason yields a skip row with that reason instead of aborting the remaining plan; tests cover strict and default validation trackers

author: claude-hub

patch.value: On a tracker with strict close validation, closeout --apply closes every eligible item with resolution, expected_result and actual_result derived only from GitHub facts and the item's own acceptance criteria. When an item has no acceptance criteria, expected_result falls back to a fixed sentence built only from GitHub facts (for example: delivered by the linked pull request, merged with its required checks passing). Generated fields never restate a defect-shaped item title as the delivered behaviour, and contain no PR body or comment text. A tracker that refuses the close for another reason yields a skip row with that reason instead of aborting the remaining plan. Tests cover strict and default validation trackers, and items with and without acceptance criteria.

message: Define the missing-criteria fallback and the defect-shaped title rule

value.author: claude-hub
value.text: Spec refinements from review: (a) CodeRabbit on PR 125: eligible in_progress items may lack acceptance criteria, so expected_result needs a fallback built only from GitHub facts, and tests must cover that case. (b) CodeRabbit on pm-rust PR 82: hand-written close fields that restated the defect-shaped title of pm-rust-poen ('Legacy list cursors without after_index publish the query fingerprint') read as if the fix shipped the defect, and had to be corrected by an appended update. Generated fields must not restate a defect-shaped title as the delivered behaviour.
